text:
Brady Tkachuk spent eight seasons in Ottawa, five as captain, before asking out and landing with his brother in Florida. Twenty-two games in, the move looks seamless: 11 goals, 23 points, 15 of them on the power play, plus 92 hits.

None of it looks borrowed. He has 10.3 expected goals (the quality of his chances), so 11 goals is about what he's earned, and Florida takes 58.6% of the five-on-five shot attempts with him on. Our wins-added measure, which credits goals by how much they swung the game, ranks him 9th of 530 skaters.

Evolving-Hockey had him driving play at the 99th percentile among forwards last season, against tough competition, though with strong teammates too. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking adds a quirk: 19% of his setups come from behind the net, against 8% for a typical forward. Goalies have to turn to find those.

The family night in St. Louis, with the Blues honoring Keith Tkachuk and his sons winning 4-1, was the headline. The steadier story is a power forward whose numbers match his reputation.
headline: Brady Tkachuk fits right in in Florida
